questions.question: Measurements indicate that the air temperature decreases by \(12^\circ \mathrm{C}\) over a vertical height of \(1,000\ \mathrm{m}\) (Environmental Lapse Rate). Comparing this to the Dry Adiabatic Lapse Rate (\(\approx 9.8^\circ \mathrm{C/km}\)), how would you classify the atmospheric stability?

A parcel of dry air rises in the atmosphere. Assuming the process is adiabatic (no heat exchange), calculate the temperature at an elevation of \(2,000\ \mathrm{m}\) if the temperature at sea level (\(0\ \mathrm{m}\)) is \(25^\circ \mathrm{C}\). Use the standard Dry Adiabatic Lapse Rate (\(\Gamma_{AD}\)).

Stack gas analysis from an incinerator shows a Carbon Dioxide (\(CO_2\)) concentration of \(8.0\%\) by volume and a Carbon Monoxide (\(CO\)) concentration of \(80\ \mathrm{ppm}\) by volume. Calculate the Combustion Efficiency (CE).

A hazardous waste incinerator is fed a POHC (Principal Organic Hazardous Contaminant) at a rate of \(500\ \mathrm{kg/h}\). The mass emission rate of the same POHC in the stack gas is measured to be \(0.04\ \mathrm{kg/h}\). Calculate the Destruction and Removal Efficiency (DRE).

An ESP is required to achieve a collection efficiency of \(99\%\) (\(\eta = 0.99\)). The gas flow rate is \(500\ \mathrm{m^3/min}\) and the particle drift velocity is \(0.1\ \mathrm{m/s}\). Calculate the required total collection area (\(A\)).

An Electrostatic Precipitator (ESP) treats an air flow of \(10,000\ \mathrm{ft^3/min}\). The total collection plate area is \(4,000\ \mathrm{ft^2}\). The effective particle drift velocity is \(0.25\ \mathrm{ft/s}\). Calculate the fractional collection efficiency.

You are designing a Pulse Jet/Felt baghouse to collect Fly Ash. According to the “Air-to-Cloth Ratio for Baghouses” table in the FE Reference Handbook, what is the typical design Air-to-Cloth ratio in \(\mathrm{m^3/(min \cdot m^2)}\)?
A cyclone has a calculated cut diameter (\(d_{pc}\)) of \(10\ \mu\mathrm{m}\). Calculate the removal efficiency for particles with a diameter (\(d_p\)) of \(20\ \mu\mathrm{m}\).

A standard cyclone is designed to remove dust from an air stream. Calculate the cut diameter (\(d_{pc}\), the particle size collected with 50% efficiency).

Given:
Inlet width \(W = 0.25\ \mathrm{m}\)

Number of effective turns \(N_e = 5\)

Inlet gas velocity \(V_i = 15\ \mathrm{m/s}\)

Particle density \(\rho_p = 1,600\ \mathrm{kg/m^3}\)

Gas density \(\rho_g = 1.2\ \mathrm{kg/m^3}\)

Gas dynamic viscosity \(\mu = 1.8 \times 10^{-5}\ \mathrm{kg/(m \cdot s)}\)

A cyclone separator has the following dimensions: Inlet height \(H = 0.5\ \mathrm{m}\), body length \(L_b = 2.0\ \mathrm{m}\), and cone length \(L_c = 2.0\ \mathrm{m}\). Calculate the number of effective turns (\(N_e\)) the gas makes in the cyclone.

An exhaust gas stream has a Carbon Monoxide (\(CO\), MW = \(28\ \mathrm{g/mol}\)) concentration of \(50\ \mathrm{ppm}\). The stack gas temperature is \(150^\circ \mathrm{C}\) and the pressure is \(1.1\ \mathrm{atm}\). Calculate the concentration in \(\mu \mathrm{g/m^3}\).

Convert a concentration of \(2.5\ \mathrm{ppm}\) of Sulfur Dioxide (\(SO_2\), MW = \(64\ \mathrm{g/mol}\)) to \(\mu \mathrm{g/m^3}\) at standard conditions (\(25^\circ \mathrm{C}\), \(1\ \mathrm{atm}\)).
Estimate the maximum parameter \((Cu/Q)_{max}\) for a source with an effective stack height \(H = 50\ \mathrm{m}\) under Stability Class D (Neutral).

A physical stack has a height of \(h = 50\ \mathrm{m}\). Due to thermal buoyancy and momentum, the plume rise is calculated to be \(\Delta h = 25\ \mathrm{m}\). What value should be used for \(H\) in the Gaussian dispersion equation?

A power plant stack emits \(SO_2\) at a rate of \(150\ \mathrm{g/s}\). The effective stack height is \(100\ \mathrm{m}\). The wind speed at stack height is \(5.0\ \mathrm{m/s}\). At a specific downwind distance, the dispersion coefficients are determined to be \(\sigma_y = 100\ \mathrm{m}\) and \(\sigma_z = 50\ \mathrm{m}\). Calculate the ground-level concentration along the plume centerline (\(y=0, z=0\)) in \(\mu \mathrm{g/m^3}\).
For a stability class of C and a downwind distance \(x\) of \(1,000\ \mathrm{m}\) , estimate the horizontal dispersion parameter (\(\sigma_y\)).
Determine the atmospheric stability class for a site with a surface wind speed of \(4.0\ \mathrm{m/s}\) during a clear summer day with strong solar insolation (sun high in the sky).

A hazardous-waste incinerator processes a liquid waste stream containing a principal organic hazardous contaminant (POHC). The mass feed rate entering the combustion chamber is \(2{,}400\ \text{kg/h}\), while the mass emission rate measured in the stack is

\(180\ \text{kg/h}\).  Determine the destruction and removal efficiency (DRE) of the incinerator.

A workshop (\(V = 200\ \mathrm{m^3}\)) has a measured steady-state toluene concentration of \(5.0\ \mathrm{mg/m^3}\). The ventilation rate is \(100\ \mathrm{m^3/h}\) and the outdoor concentration is \(0.5\ \mathrm{mg/m^3}\). Assuming conservative behavior (\(k=0\)), back-calculate the indoor source generation rate (\(S\)).
questions.officialSubtopic: Quality management, planning, assurance, and systems

questions.question: In an HVAC system, the return air has a \(CO_2\) concentration of \(800\ \mathrm{ppm}\), and the outdoor air has a concentration of \(400\ \mathrm{ppm}\). The supply air (mixed air) delivered to the room has a measured concentration of \(500\ \mathrm{ppm}\). Calculate the percentage of outdoor air (% Outdoor Air) in the supply stream.
questions.officialSubtopic: Quality management, planning, assurance, and systems

questions.question: A conference room is designed for 20 people. Each person exhales Carbon Dioxide (\(CO_2\)) at a rate of \(0.3\ \mathrm{L/min}\). The outdoor \(CO_2\) concentration is \(400\ \mathrm{ppm}\). If the indoor \(CO_2\) concentration must not exceed \(1,000\ \mathrm{ppm}\), calculate the minimum required ventilation rate (\(Q\)) per person.
questions.officialSubtopic: Quality management, planning, assurance, and systems

questions.question: A classroom has dimensions of \(10\ \mathrm{m} \times 8\ \mathrm{m} \times 3\ \mathrm{m}\). The ventilation system supplies air at a rate of \(120\ \mathrm{m^3/h}\). Calculate the Air Changes per Hour.
questions.officialSubtopic: Quality management, planning, assurance, and systems

questions.question: Formaldehyde is being emitted in a room (\(V = 100\ \mathrm{m^3}\)) at a rate of \(S = 20\ \mathrm{mg/h}\). Ventilation rate is \(Q = 50\ \mathrm{m^3/h}\). Outdoor concentration \(C_o = 0\). Decay rate \(k = 0.2\ \mathrm{h^{-1}}\). Calculate steady-state concentration.
questions.officialSubtopic: Quality management, planning, assurance, and systems

questions.question: An environmental engineer is assessing a spill of Kerosene that occurred on a site characterized by Coarse Gravel. The spill volume is estimated to be \(1.5\ \mathrm{m^3}\) spread over an area of \(5\ \mathrm{m^2}\). Calculate the maximum depth of penetration for this spill.

A volume of \(2.0\ \mathrm{m^3}\) of gasoline is spilled onto a ground surface consisting of “Coarse to Medium Sand”. The spill covers a surface area of \(10\ \mathrm{m^2}\). Estimate the maximum vertical depth of penetration (\(D\)) into the vadose zone.

A Completely Mixed Flow Reactor (CMFR/CSTR) has an influent pollutant concentration of \(100\ \mathrm{mg/L}\) and a hydraulic residence time (\( \theta \)) of \(4\ \mathrm{hours}\). The pollutant decays via a first-order reaction with a rate constant \(k = 0.25\ \mathrm{h^{-1}}\). Calculate the steady-state effluent concentration.
tags: Steady State Reactor Parameters Constant Density Systems

questions.question: Calculate the Retardation Factor (\(R\)) for a contaminant in groundwater. The soil bulk density (\(\rho_b\)) is \(1.5\ \mathrm{kg/L}\) , the porosity (\(n_e\)) is \(0.30\), and the distribution coefficient (\(K_d\)) is \(2.0\ \mathrm{L/kg}\).
Calculate the Soil-Water Partition Coefficient (\(K_sw\)) for a chemical with \(K_{oc} = 1,200\ \mathrm{L/kg}\) in a sediment with an organic carbon content of \(0.5\%\) (\(f_{oc} = 0.005\)).

A soil sample has a Soil-Water Partition Coefficient (\(K_{sw}\)) of \(20\ \mathrm{L/kg}\). The fraction of organic carbon in the soil (\(f_{oc}\)) is \(0.04\) (\(4\%\)). Calculate the Organic Carbon Partition Coefficient (\(K_{oc}\)).

The Octanol-Water Partition Coefficient (\(K_{ow}\)) is used to determine the hydrophobicity of a chemical. If the equilibrium concentration of a chemical in the octanol phase is \(150\ \mathrm{mg/L}\) and in the water phase is \(0.5\ \mathrm{mg/L}\), calculate \(K_{ow}\).

A chemical substance has an equilibrium concentration of \(20\ \mathrm{mg/kg}\) in fish tissue and \(0.05\ \mathrm{mg/L}\) in the surrounding water. Calculate the Bioconcentration Factor (BCF) in \(\mathrm{L/kg}\).

The deoxygenation rate constant (\(k_d\)) is determined to be \(0.20\ \mathrm{day^{-1}}\) at \(20^\circ \mathrm{C}\). Calculate the rate constant at \(10^\circ \mathrm{C}\) using a temperature coefficient (\(\theta\)) of \(1.047\).

A wastewater sample has an ultimate BOD (\(L_0\)) of \(250\ \mathrm{mg/L}\). The deoxygenation rate constant (\(k\)) is \(0.23\ \mathrm{day^{-1}}\) (base e). Calculate the amount of BOD exerted in 5 days.

A wastewater sample has an ultimate BOD (\(L_0\)) of \(250\ \mathrm{mg/L}\). The deoxygenation rate constant (\(k\)) is \(0.23\ \mathrm{day^{-1}}\) (base e). Calculate the remaining BOD (\(L_t\)) after 3 days.

Using the Streeter-Phelps equation, the oxygen deficit (\(D_t\)) at \(t = 2\ \mathrm{days}\) is calculated to be \(3.5\ \mathrm{mg/L}\). If the saturation dissolved oxygen concentration (\(DO_{sat}\)) for the stream is \(9.0\ \mathrm{mg/L}\), what is the actual Dissolved Oxygen (DO) concentration at this time?

For a stream with the following characteristics, calculate the critical time (\(t_c\)) at which the minimum dissolved oxygen occurs.
Deoxygenation rate constant, \(k_d = 0.2\ \mathrm{day^{-1}}\)

Reaeration rate constant, \(k_r = 0.4\ \mathrm{day^{-1}}\)

Initial Ultimate BOD, \(L_a = 20\ \mathrm{mg/L}\)

Initial Deficit, \(D_a = 0\ \mathrm{mg/L}\) (Saturated)

A river flows at \(5.0\ \mathrm{m^3/s}\) with an ultimate BOD (\(L_r\)) of \(3.0\ \mathrm{mg/L}\). A wastewater treatment plant discharges \(0.2\ \mathrm{m^3/s}\) of effluent with an ultimate BOD (\(L_w\)) of \(50.0\ \mathrm{mg/L}\). Calculate the initial ultimate BOD (\(L_a\)) of the mixed stream just downstream of the discharge.

A wastewater stream with a flow of \(Q_w = 0.5\ \mathrm{m^3/s}\) and a Dissolved Oxygen (DO) concentration of \(2.0\ \mathrm{mg/L}\) discharges into a river. The river has a flow of \(Q_r = 3.0\ \mathrm{m^3/s}\) and a DO concentration of \(8.5\ \mathrm{mg/L}\). If the saturation DO concentration (\(DO_{sat}\)) at the mixture temperature is \(9.2\ \mathrm{mg/L}\), calculate the initial oxygen deficit (\(D_a\)).

Microbial growth in a reactor follows Monod kinetics. The maximum specific growth rate (\(\mu_{max}\)) is \(3.0\ \mathrm{day^{-1}}\) and the half-velocity constant (\(K_s\)) is \(40\ \mathrm{mg/L}\). If the substrate concentration (\(S\)) is \(20\ \mathrm{mg/L}\) and the endogenous decay coefficient (\(k_d\)) is \(0.05\ \mathrm{day^{-1}}\), what is the specific growth rate (\(\mu\))?

A landfill engineer needs to estimate the in-place density of solid waste at a specific depth. The waste was initially compacted to a specific weight of \(SW_i = 1,000\ \mathrm{lb/yd^3}\). At the depth of interest, the overburden pressure is \(p = 10\ \mathrm{lb/in^2}\). Using the empirical compaction constants \(a = 0.01\ \mathrm{yd^3/in^2}\) and \(b = 0.05\ \mathrm{yd^3/lb}\), calculate the specific weight (\(SW_p\)) of the waste at this depth.

Annual monitoring data for a landfill final cover system is collected to perform a water balance analysis. The recorded components are as follows:
Precipitation: \(30\ \mathrm{in.}\)

Surface Runoff: \(5\ \mathrm{in.}\)

Evapotranspiration: \(20\ \mathrm{in.}\)

Percolation through the cover: \(2\ \mathrm{in.}\)
Calculate the change in soil moisture storage (\(\Delta S_{LC}\)) for the landfill cover.

Calculate the gas flux (\(N_A\)) through a landfill cover.

Given:
Diffusion coefficient \(D = 18.6\ \mathrm{ft^2/d}\)

Porosity \(\eta = 0.4\)

Concentration difference \(\Delta C = 0.005\ \mathrm{lb\text{-}mol/ft^3}\)

Cover depth \(L = 3\ \mathrm{ft}\)

Calculate the breakthrough time (\(t\)) for leachate to penetrate a clay liner. The liner thickness is \(d = 2\ \mathrm{ft}\), porosity \(\eta = 0.2\), and hydraulic head \(h = 2\ \mathrm{ft}\). The hydraulic conductivity is \(K = 0.01\ \mathrm{ft/yr}\).
What is the typical density of Clear Glass (whole bottles) in the category of as-received source-separated materials?
Which component has the highest typical moisture content?

Solid waste is compacted in a landfill. The initial volume of the waste is \(V_i = 100\ \mathrm{yd^3}\), and the final volume after compaction is \(V_f = 20\ \mathrm{yd^3}\). Calculate the percent volume reduction.

A 2 ft thick clay with permeability of 8 ft/yr is used as a liner material for a landfill project. The porosity of the clay is 0.4. If the hydraulic head is 10 ft, the time in days it may take for the leachate material to penetrate the liner is most nearly:
tags: Break Through Time For Leachate To Penetrate A Clay Liner

questions.question: A population grows by “Percent Growth” method. If the population grows from 100 to 121 in 2 periods (\(n=2\)), what is the growth rate \(k\)?

Using the Ratio and Correlation Growth method, calculate the projected population of a city (\(P_2\)).
Given:
City population at last census (\(P_1\)) = 10,000

Region population at last census (\(P_{1R}\)) = 100,000

Projected region population (\(P_{2R}\)) = 150,000

Assume the ratio \(k\) remains constant.
A population is growing according to the Log Growth (Exponential) model. If \(P_0 = 100,000\) and \(k = 0.02\ \mathrm{year^{-1}}\). What is the population after 10 years?

Use the Linear Projection model to predict the population in year 2030.

Given: \(P_{2010} = 50,000\) and \(k = 1,500\ \mathrm{people/year}\).

Consider a radioactive decay chain where a parent isotope decays into a daughter isotope, which is also radioactive and decays further. The decay constant for the parent is \(\lambda_1 = 0.1\ \mathrm{d^{-1}}\) and the decay constant for the daughter is \(\lambda_2 = 0.2\ \mathrm{d^{-1}}\). Assuming the initial population of the daughter isotope is zero, at what time (\(t\)) does the activity of the daughter product reach its maximum?

During a routine site survey, a radiation safety officer measures an exposure rate of \(I_1 = 100\ \mathrm{mR/h}\) at a distance of \(R_1 = 5\ \mathrm{m}\) from a point source of gamma radiation. To reduce exposure, the officer moves to a new location at a distance of \(R_2 = 10\ \mathrm{m}\) from the source. What is the expected radiation intensity at this new distance?

A health physicist is assessing the internal exposure of a worker who accidentally inhaled a radionuclide. The radionuclide has a physical (radioactive) half-life (\(\tau_r\)) of \(8\ \mathrm{days}\). Medical testing determines that the worker’s body clears the substance with a biological half-life (\(\tau_b\)) of \(24\ \mathrm{days}\). Calculate the effective half-life (\(\tau_e\)) of the radionuclide in the worker’s body.
A radioactive isotope decays according to first-order kinetics with a rate constant \(k = 0.05\ \mathrm{year^{-1}}\). Calculate the half-life (\(t_{1/2}\)) of this isotope.

An environmental engineer is establishing Data Quality Objectives (DQOs) for a site investigation. The established background mean concentration for a contaminant is \(\mu_B = 100\ \mathrm{mg/kg}\). The investigation is designed to detect contamination if the site mean concentration reaches \(\mu_S = 120\ \mathrm{mg/kg}\). Calculate the Minimum Detectable Relative Difference.
questions.officialSubtopic: Quality management, planning, assurance, and systems

questions.question: An environmental engineer is designing a soil sampling plan to demonstrate compliance with a cleanup standard. Preliminary data suggests the site has a Coefficient of Variation (CV) of \(25\%\). The Data Quality Objectives (DQO) specify a \(95\%\) Confidence Level and a \(95\%\) Power to detect a Minimum Detectable Relative Difference of \(20\%\). Determine the minimum number of samples required.
questions.officialSubtopic: Quality management, planning, assurance, and systems

questions.question: An environmental engineer is developing a sampling plan for an Emergency Cleanup operation following a hazardous spill. To ensure the data quality meets standard objectives without imposing excessive sampling costs typical of long-term remediation, what is the appropriate target range for the Confidence Level (\(1 – \alpha\))?
questions.officialSubtopic: Quality management, planning, assurance, and systems

questions.question: An environmental engineer is analyzing a set of soil samples for lead contamination. The laboratory results indicate a mean concentration (\(\bar{x}\)) of \(50\ \mathrm{mg/kg}\) with a standard deviation (\(s\)) of \(10\ \mathrm{mg/kg}\). What is the Coefficient of Variation (CV)?
questions.officialSubtopic: Estimation, confidence intervals, and hypothesis testing

questions.question: An activated sludge system is designed using the “Extended Aeration” process modification. What is the typical range for the Mean Cell Residence Time (\(\theta_c\))?

An extended aeration activated sludge plant treats a flow of \(4,000\ \mathrm{m^3/day}\) with an influent BOD\(_5\) of \(250\ \mathrm{mg/L}\). Estimate the required air supply range in \(\mathrm{m^3/day}\).

A wastewater treatment plant has an aeration tank volume of \(1.5\ \mathrm{MG}\) and operates at an MLSS of \(3,000\ \mathrm{mg/L}\). The target mean cell residence time (\(\theta_c\)) is \(8\ \mathrm{days}\). The waste activated sludge (WAS) concentration is \(8,000\ \mathrm{mg/L}\). Assuming the effluent suspended solids are negligible (\(X_e \approx 0\)), calculate the required WAS flow rate \(Q_w\) in MGD.

An activated sludge aeration tank has a volume of \(2,000\ \mathrm{m^3}\). The mixed liquor suspended solids (MLSS) concentration is maintained at \(3,500\ \mathrm{mg/L}\). If the operator maintains a mean cell residence time (\(\theta_c\)) of \(10\ \mathrm{days}\), what is the total sludge production rate (solids wasted + effluent solids) in kg/day?

A \(1.0\ \mathrm{L}\) sample of mixed liquor from an aeration tank is allowed to settle for 30 minutes in a graduated cylinder. The volume of the settled sludge is found to be \(250\ \mathrm{mL}\). The mixed liquor suspended solids (MLSS) concentration is \(2,500\ \mathrm{mg/L}\). Calculate the Sludge Volume Index (SVI).

An aeration tank with a volume of \(5,000\ \mathrm{m^3}\) receives a wastewater flow of \(15,000\ \mathrm{m^3/day}\). The influent BOD is \(300\ \mathrm{mg/L}\). Calculate the Organic Loading Rate (Volumetric) in \(\mathrm{kg\ BOD/m^3 \cdot day}\).

A treatment plant receives a flow of \(10\ \mathrm{MGD}\) with a BOD concentration of \(180\ \mathrm{mg/L}\). The aeration basin has a volume of \(150,000\ \mathrm{ft^3}\). The MLVSS concentration is \(3,000\ \mathrm{mg/L}\). The F:M ratio (\(\mathrm{lb\ BOD/lb\ MLVSS \cdot day}\)) is most nearly:

An activated sludge plant has an influent flow of \(2,500\ \mathrm{m^3/day}\) with a BOD\(_5\) of \(200\ \mathrm{mg/L}\). The aeration tank has a volume of \(1,000\ \mathrm{m^3}\). The Mixed Liquor Volatile Suspended Solids (MLVSS) concentration is \(2,000\ \mathrm{mg/L}\). Calculate the Food-to-Microorganism (F:M) ratio in \(day^{-1}\).

A wastewater treatment plant treats a flow of \(5.0\ \mathrm{MGD}\). The aeration tank volume is \(1.5\ \mathrm{MG}\) and the MLSS is \(2,500\ \mathrm{mg/L}\). The waste sludge flow rate (\(Q_w\)) is \(0.05\ \mathrm{MGD}\) with a concentration of \(8,000\ \mathrm{mg/L}\). The effluent suspended solids concentration (\(X_e\)) is \(15\ \mathrm{mg/L}\). The solids residence time (\(\theta_c\)) is most nearly:

An activated sludge aeration tank has a volume of \(4,000\ \mathrm{m^3}\). The mixed liquor suspended solids (MLSS) concentration is maintained at \(3,000\ \mathrm{mg/L}\). The total sludge production (solids wasted plus solids lost in the effluent) is determined to be \(2,400\ \mathrm{kg/day}\). The Solids residence time  (\(\theta_c\)) in days is most nearly:

A \( 150,000 \, \mathrm{L} \) activated sludge reactor receives an influent wastewater flow rate of \( 1,500 \, \mathrm{L/min} \) with an influent \( \mathrm{BOD_5} \) concentration of \( 220 \, \mathrm{mg/L} \). The mixed liquor volatile suspended solids (MLVSS) concentration in the reactor is \( 3,200 \, \mathrm{mg/L} \). The food-to-microorganism (\( \mathrm{F:M} \)) ratio of the system is most nearly:

A \( 900,000 \)-gallon conventional activated sludge process has a recycle ratio of \( 0.30 \), an influent flow rate of \( 1.2 \, \mathrm{MGD} \), a mixed liquor volatile suspended solids (MLVSS) concentration of \( 800 \, \mathrm{mg/L} \), and an influent \( \mathrm{BOD_5} \) of \( 180 \, \mathrm{mg/L} \). The F:M ratio of the process is most nearly:

A \( 32 \, \mathrm{m} \) diameter clarifier has a flow rate \( Q = 6 \, \mathrm{MGD} \) and a biomass concentration \( X_A = 180 \, \mathrm{mg/L} \). Determine the solids loading rate (\( \mathrm{SLR} \)). The solids loading rate is most nearly:

Adsorption data follows the Langmuir isotherm. The saturation capacity (\(a\)) is \(50\ \mathrm{mg/g}\) and the constant \(K\) is \(0.1\ \mathrm{L/mg}\). Calculate the solid phase concentration (\(x/m\)) when the equilibrium liquid concentration (\(C_e\)) is \(20\ \mathrm{mg/L}\).

Adsorption data for an organic pollutant follows the Freundlich isotherm. The constants are \(K = 2.0\ (\mathrm{mg/g})(L/mg)^{1/n}\) and \(1/n = 0.5\). If the equilibrium concentration (\(C_e\)) is \(16\ \mathrm{mg/L}\), calculate the mass of solute adsorbed per unit mass of adsorbent (\(x/m\)).

A reverse osmosis system operates with a transmembrane pressure difference (\(\Delta P\)) of \(3,000\ \mathrm{kPa}\) and an osmotic pressure differential (\(\Delta \pi\)) of \(400\ \mathrm{kPa}\). The water permeation coefficient (\(W_p\)) is \(1.5 \times 10^{-6}\ \mathrm{kmol/(m^2 \cdot s \cdot kPa)}\). Calculate the water flux (\(J_w\)).

Calculate the osmotic pressure (\(\Pi\)) of a solution containing \(0.1\ \mathrm{mol/m^3}\) of NaCl at \(25^\circ \mathrm{C}\) (\(298\ \mathrm{K}\)). Assume complete dissociation (\(v=2\)) and an osmotic coefficient (\(\Phi\)) of \(1.0\).
(Use \(R = 8,314\ \mathrm{Pa \cdot m^3/(kmol \cdot K)}\))

In an air stripping packed tower design, the Height of a Transfer Unit (HTU) is calculated to be \(1.2\ \mathrm{m}\). The required Number of Transfer Units (NTU) to achieve 99% removal is determined to be \(4.5\). Calculate the total packing height (\(Z\)).

An air stripping tower is designed with a dimensionless Henry’s constant \(H’ = 0.25\). The design calls for a Stripping Factor (\(R_S\)) of \(5.0\). Calculate the required volumetric air-to-water ratio (\(Q_A/Q_W\)).

A contaminant has a Henry’s Law constant (\(H\)) of \(0.01\ \mathrm{atm \cdot m^3/kmol}\) at \(20^\circ \mathrm{C}\). Calculate the dimensionless Henry’s Law constant (\(H’\)).
(Use \(R = 0.0821\ \mathrm{m^3 \cdot atm/(kmol \cdot K)}\))

Alum (\(Al_2(SO_4)_3 \cdot 14H_2O\), MW \(\approx 594\)) is added to water at a dose of \(30\ \mathrm{mg/L}\). Based on the coagulation stoichiometry, how much alkalinity (expressed as \(CaCO_3\)) is consumed?

A sample of water has a Calcium Non-Carbonate Hardness (Permanent Hardness) of \(80\ \mathrm{mg/L}\) as \(CaCO_3\). Calculate the theoretical amount of Soda Ash (\(Na_2CO_3\)) required to remove this hardness.
(MW data: \(CaCO_3 = 100.1\), \(Na_2CO_3 = 106.0\))

A water source contains \(1.5\ \mathrm{mmol/L}\) of Magnesium Carbonate Hardness (\(Mg(HCO_3)_2\)). Calculate the stoichiometric amount of hydrated lime (\(Ca(OH)_2\), MW = \(74.1\ \mathrm{g/mol}\)) required to remove this magnesium.

Water analysis indicates a Calcium Carbonate Hardness of \(2.0\ \mathrm{mmol/L}\) (as \(Ca^{2+}\)). How much hydrated lime (\(Ca(OH)_2\), MW = \(74.1\ \mathrm{g/mol}\)) is required to remove this hardness stoichiometrically?

During the backwash of a rapid sand filter, the backwash velocity (\(v_B\)) is set to \(15\ \mathrm{m/hr}\). The terminal settling velocity (\(v_t\)) of the sand particles is determined to be \(180\ \mathrm{m/hr}\). Calculate the porosity of the fluidized bed (\(\eta_f\)).

A rapid sand filter has a bed depth of \(0.7\ \mathrm{m}\). The filtration rate (approach velocity) is \(300\ \mathrm{m/day}\). The sand grains have a diameter of \(0.6\ \mathrm{mm}\) and a drag coefficient (\(C_D\)) of \(5.0\). The porosity of the bed is \(0.4\). Using the Rose equation, calculate the head loss through the clean filter bed.

Determine the required CT value for 3-log (99.9%) inactivation of Giardia cysts by free chlorine under the following conditions:
Temperature: \(\le 0.5^\circ \mathrm{C}\)

pH: \(7.5\)

Chlorine Concentration: \(1.0\ \mathrm{mg/L}\)

A chlorine contact basin has a volume of \(20,000\ \mathrm{gallons}\) and the peak hourly flow rate is \(400\ \mathrm{gpm}\). The basin is classified as having “Superior” baffling conditions (\(BF = 0.7\)). Calculate the \(t_{10}\) time.

A disinfection process uses free chlorine. The residual chlorine concentration measured during peak hourly flow is \(1.5\ \mathrm{mg/L}\). The contact time \(t_{10}\) (time for 10% of water to pass) is determined to be \(90\ \mathrm{minutes}\). Calculate the \(CT_{calc}\) value.

A particle is settling in water with a calculated terminal velocity of \(0.1\ \mathrm{m/s}\). The particle diameter is \(0.5\ \mathrm{mm}\) (\(5 \times 10^{-4}\ \mathrm{m}\)). The kinematic viscosity of water is \(\nu = 1 \times 10^{-6}\ \mathrm{m^2/s}\). Calculate the Reynolds number and determine the flow regime.

A spherical sand particle with a diameter of \(0.1\ \mathrm{mm}\) (\(1 \times 10^{-4}\ \mathrm{m}\)) and a density of \(2,650\ \mathrm{kg/m^3}\) is settling in water at \(20^\circ \mathrm{C}\). The water density is \(\rho_f = 998\ \mathrm{kg/m^3}\) and the dynamic viscosity is \(\mu = 1.002 \times 10^{-3}\ \mathrm{Pa \cdot s}\). Assuming laminar flow (Stokes’ Law applies), calculate the terminal settling velocity.
